title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: transverse vibrations of an elastic rod (virga) of length a, governed by the Euler–Bernoulli equation. The time factor is sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)). The space factor is y(s) = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f), with f^4 = bcck.

Boundary conditions:
- From the preceding pages, γ = α − β and δ = α + β. These are equivalent to y'' = y''' = 0 at s = 0, i.e. a free end.
- At s = a (u = 1, ω = a/f), y = 0 and y'' = 0, i.e. a simply supported (pinned) end.

Frequency equation: eliminating α/β gives p e^{-ω} + q e^{ω} = 0 with p = sin ω + cos ω and q = sin ω − cos ω. This is tan ω = tanh ω.

This page:
- Euler substitutes sin ω, cos ω = ±(e^ω ∓ e^{-ω})/√(2(e^{2ω} + e^{-2ω})). In both sign cases α/β = −e^{-2ω}.
- Taking α = 1 gives β = −e^{2ω}, γ = 1 + e^{2ω}, δ = 1 − e^{2ω}.
- With u = s/a the mode is y = C sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)) [e^{uω} − e^{(2−u)ω} + (1 + e^{2ω}) sin uω + (1 − e^{2ω}) cos uω].
- From f = a/ω: k = a^4/(bcc ω^4) and √(2g/k) = ω²c√(2gb)/a². The 'oscillation' time (Euler's half-period convention) is π a²/(ω² c√(2gb)), and the pitch is ω² c√(2gb)/(π a²).
- Everything is thus reduced to the roots of tan ω = tanh ω. The root ω = 0 is trivial (no motion), so Euler sets up a quadrant-by-quadrant search.

On the next page Euler finds no root in quadrant 1 or in the even quadrants. The first root is ω ≈ 5π/4 − Φ with tan Φ ≈ e^{-5π/2} ≈ 1/2576, i.e. ω ≈ 3.9266, which matches the modern value.
errors: Printed misprint in the 'posteriore casu' line: −1/e^{2ω} is equated to −e^{−ω}; it should be −e^{−2ω}. The preceding case and the subsequent β = −e^{2ω} confirm the intended value.
Typographic: the formula printed as '√2g/k' means √(2g/k).
The period π√(k/2g) is a half-period of sin(t√(2g/k)). This is consistent with Euler's convention of counting single swings, not an error.

ideas.what: Mode shape and frequency equation tan ω = tanh ω for a rod free at one end and pinned at the other.
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Bernoulli beam eigenvalue problem, free–pinned (equivalently clamped–pinned eigenvalues) boundary conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1740s); systematized by Rayleigh's Theory of Sound
ideas.where_published: E526 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1779 [1782]); earlier beam vibration work in E65 Additamentum I (1744); see Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11.2)

ideas.what: Pitch formula ν = ω² c√(2gb)/(π a²): frequency ∝ thickness/length² with eigenvalue factor ω².
ideas.modern_name: Beam natural frequency scaling ω_n = λ_n² √(EI/(ρA L^4))
ideas.where_published: E526; also earlier Euler and Bernoulli papers on the sounds of rods

ideas.what: Root location of tan ω = tanh ω by quadrant analysis, using power series in the first quadrant.
ideas.modern_name: Transcendental eigenvalue equation root bracketing; asymptotics λ_n ≈ (4n+1)π/4

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, standard derivation of the free–pinned beam modes and frequency equation, well documented in Truesdell's account of E526. The only item of note is a minor printed misprint (−e^{−ω} for −e^{−2ω}).
transcription_corrections: The transcription faithfully reproduces the printed '−1/e^{2ω} = −e^{−ω}'; the original contains this misprint and the intended value is −e^{−2ω}.
